items.title: Square Enix is working on improvements for the "prolonged" loading times of Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2
items.summary: A fix is in the pipeline with the problem causing the issue already identified.
items.content:
0 Copied! Copied! Comment now! Subscribe to our newsletter here! * Required field E-mail * Name * --> HQ initPlayerScript('803103'); Worry no longer, Final Fantasy XIV players on Nintendo Switch 2, Square Enix is hard at work on a fix for the lengthy loading times currently affecting this version of the game. As confirmed in a post on The Lodestone website , the issue has been identified with a solution already being tested, meaning a rollout is likely close at hand.

Square Enix talks about the issue as "prolonged transition screens" , and has recognised these appear when teleporting to a different map in an instanced duty, when the screen fades to black during a battle phase transition, when the screen fades the black after being knocked out, and when the screen fades to black after using Return or a shortcut.

The good news is the reason for this problem has been determined to be related to "data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time" . As this has been identified, the processes have been optimised to "ensure faster data loading even under similar conditions, and the updated version is currently in testing."

Signing off, Square Enix explains: "We are working to release an update as soon as possible to address this and several other issues. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your understanding in the meantime."

It's unclear as to exactly when this fix will be introduced.

items.title: PSA: Final Fantasy XIV Getting Switch 2 Update To Address Prolonged Loading
items.summary: An updated version is already in testing
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Online is out now for the Switch 2, and like all good MMO launches, it seems there are some teething issues.

Square Enix has identified a prolonged loading bug in this version of the game, with a notice on the official game website detailing how it "may take longer than usual" when the screen fades to black in instanced duties.

Here's part of the official notice and what Switch 2 players may experience:

[Nintendo Switch 2] Regarding Prolonged Transition Screens (Aug. 4)

Our investigation has confirmed that, when a player enters an instanced duty while surrounded by many characters, loading data will take longer than usual, which lasts until the player leaves the instance. The delay is especially noticeable in the following situations: ・When the screen fades to black during a battle phase transition or when teleporting to a different map in an instanced duty ・When the screen fades to black upon reviving after being K.O.'d in an instanced duty ・When the screen fades to black upon using Return or a shortcut in an instanced duty We have identified certain cases in which the data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time. As such, these processes have been optimised to ensure faster data loading even under similar conditions, and the updated version is currently in testing.

Fortunately, as mentioned, an updated version is already in the works, and the team is aiming to release it as "soon as possible" to address this problem, as well as "several other issues".

Have you encountered this loading issue? How has your experience been with FFXIV on the Switch 2 so far? Let us know in the comments.

items.title: Square Enix details loading times issue with Final Fantasy 14 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Square Enix has identified a loading times issue with the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14. The company says that “loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.” An update is planned to address the issue. It seems that the origin of the problem stems from entering “a content area while...
items.content:
Square Enix has identified a loading times issue with the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14.

The company says that “loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.” An update is planned to address the issue.

It seems that the origin of the problem stems from entering “a content area while surrounded by a large number of characters”. Square Enix says that “in some cases, the data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time.” The upcoming update will further improve optimization.

The full notice regarding Final Fantasy 14’s Nintendo Switch 2 loading issue is as follows:

We have confirmed that in the Nintendo Switch 2 version, loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.

Our investigation has confirmed that when players enter a content area while surrounded by a large number of characters, loading times within that content take longer than usual from the moment they enter until they exit. When this issue occurs, the delay is particularly noticeable in the following situations:

Regarding this issue, we have confirmed that in some cases, the data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time. We have therefore further optimized these processes to ensure faster data loading even under similar conditions, and we are currently testing the updated program.

We are working to release an update as soon as possible to address this and several other issues, so we ask for your patience until the issue is resolved.

Final Fantasy 14 is up on the Nintendo eShop. We have information about subscription fees, a perk for Nintendo Switch Online members, and more here .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Coins Used for FFXIV Switch 2 Subscriptions
items.summary: You can only buy Final Fantasy XIV Switch 2 subscriptions and some other items with the new FFXIV Coins currency.
items.content:
Square Enix went over the new Final Fantasy XIV Coins currency used for things like subscriptions that the Switch 2 version of FFXIV and its expansions through Dawntrail are available. These will be purchased from the eShop. However, as the subscription will be waved for about a month after launch as the company ensures the MMORPG is running properly, that currency will only be used for account services and Online Store optional items at the moment. No Nintendo Switch Online subscription is required to play, though there is a perk for people who have one and are going through the game.

Square Enix didn’t explain what the exchange rate will be for FFXIV Coins on the Switch 2 in its announcement. It only noted that will be the way people will need to pay for things tied to real money in the MMORPG. When someone buys them on the eShop, they will be credited to a Square Enix Account. Those could then be used on Mog Station or to get things like mounts, cosmetics, Home World Transfer Services, Character Renaming Services, Fantasia, or Tales of Adventure in the Online Store . It also noted that, in order to be sure the currency shows in your account, someone would need to close the MMORPG after buying them and log in again.

The Nintendo Switch Online Perk doesn’t require any additional in-game actions or purchases. The bonus lets someone get another free Aetheryte as a free destination. This means one more place someone could teleport to without paying gil.

As a reminder, multiple versions of FFXIV are available on the Switch 2 at launch and don’t initially require a subscriptions to play. The base game is $19.99. There is also a Complete Edition for $59.99 that includes all expansions and Dawntrail. The Complete Collector’s Edition is $139.99 and goes up through Dawntrail and has all of the original collector’s edition items from the main MMORPG and expansions.

Final Fantasy XIV is available for the PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC, the Switch 2 version arrives on August 4, 2026, and the new expansion FFXIV Evercold debuts in January 2027.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Switch 2 Launch Is a Surprise Success With One Huge Catch
items.summary: Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate
items.content:
Listen Thread 2 Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Aug 4, 2026, 10:33 AM EDT News Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate

Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players Pokémon studio's new game arrives on Xbox Game Pass today Rust's major August update is concerning for solo players Final Fantasy 14's Switch 2 launch is going better than expected, mostly Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Warriors of Light can finally explore Eorzea on the Nintendo Switch 2 . On Tuesday, Aug. 4, Square Enix finally released Final Fantasy 14 on the hybrid console-handheld. For the most part, players report that things are going pretty well!

This marks the beginning of what Square Enix is calling a one-month early access period for Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2. During this time, players can enjoy everything the critically acclaimed MMORPG has to offer just as they would on any other platform. Square Enix will not enforce the game's subscription requirement during the first month on Switch 2. Regardless of whether you are a new or returning player, you can enjoy Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2 entirely for free during the early access period.

There is a caveat to this good news. When the early access period does end, subscriptions will be required and there's a special Nintendo tax . Typically, Warriors of Light pay for a single subscription that works for all platforms the MMO is available on. The Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14 , however, will require its own subscription, even for those who have active subscriptions already.

To mitigate the extra cost, Square Enix is offering Switch 2 subscriptions at half price for players with existing subscriptions. Furthermore, players do not need a Nintendo Switch Online subscription to play the online game. The complete edition of Final Fantasy 14 , which includes all currently released expansions, is also on sale for a limited time at a discount of 30%. Though if you are just curious to try the MMO, start by downloading the free trial. Once you purchase the game in any way, you can't use the free trial without creating a new account entirely.

Even with all the extra hoops to jump through on Switch 2, players are reporting that the game is running very smoothly. Some Warriors of Light, eager to test out just how much the console can handle, went directly to the Limsa Lominsa Aetheryte Plaza, one of the consistently busiest locations in the game. In handheld mode, the Switch 2 was able to perform admirably in this rendering gauntlet. If performance was players' biggest worry before the Switch 2 release, today's launch has assuaged those concerns. Most reactions on social media are just sharing their awe that the game runs as well as it does.

That isn't to say the launch has been without hiccups. Some players are posting excessively long download times. While the game's 117 GB is nothing to sneeze at, waiting over a dozen hours for the download to complete seems excessive. Of course, this could be caused by individual network issues and not a platform problem. The biggest issue players are facing is getting the game to work with existing accounts.

There are already a couple posts on the Final Fantasy 14 subreddit asking for help troubleshooting the complex setup process on Switch 2. Hopefully these are just growing pains of launching the MMO on a new platform and Square Enix will sort it out soon enough. The game is technically still in an early access period on Switch 2. Players can follow a detailed guide on how to set up the game on Switch 2 on the Final Fantasy 14 blog .

Overall, feedback has been resoundingly positive for the Switch 2 launch. At the very least, it gives curious players who have never tried the beloved MMO a perfect reason to finally see what all the fuss is about before the Evercold expansion is released in January.

items.title: PSA: Final Fantasy 14 Is Out Now On Nintendo Switch 2 But You Don't Have To Buy It To Play
items.summary: Hope you have that meme memorized because it's relevant again; something something free trial something something
items.content:
By now, if you’re a Final Fantasy XIV player, you’re sick of the copypasta that starts, “ Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV ? ” But loathe as I am to invoke a meme that’s long, long been run into the ground…it’s actually relevant again. Final Fantasy XIV is out on the Nintendo Switch 2 today. And if you’re one of the folks interested in trying the critically acclaimed MMORPG on the go, you may be tempted to buy one of the versions that’s now on sale at 30 percent off.

But you shouldn’t. Because, as the meme is so fond of reminding us, there’s a free trial available . And over the years, as the game has grown through expansions, the free trial expanded too. Now, instead of just getting A Realm Reborn and Heavensward and being able to play up to level 60, you get access to Stormblood and Shadowbringers too, bringing the character level cap up to 80. The freebies also include access to all the job classes released with the expansions: Machinist, Astrologian, Dancer, Dark Knight, Red Mage, Gunbreaker, and Samurai.

After you’ve reached the end of Shadowbringers , the next purchase step is the Final Fantasy XIV Complete Edition which includes the latest expansions, Endwalker and Dawntrail . Once you purchase any license for the game, you get 30 days of subscription time for free before you’ll be forced to kick out money for a monthly subscription. Players who have an active subscription on another platform will have to buy a new one (at half price) for the Switch 2, and a separate license. But one perk of playing FFXIV on the Nintendo Switch 2 (and the Playstation 5 for that matter) is that you don’t need to pay for an additional online subscription to play like you do on Xbox .

The free trial does come with certain restrictions. For example, chat commands are limited, you won’t have access to everything in the online store, you’ll be allowed a maximum of 300,000 gil (in-game currency), and a big one— you won’t be able to create your own party but you can be invited to a party or join one in the dungeon queue. Check out the full list of what’s allowed and what’s not here to plan you free-trial trip through Eorzea accordingly.
